patch_description:
Replace the cube--octahedron compound by a deterministic numerical construction of seven optimally spread unoriented lines in three-dimensional space, returning both antipodal endpoints of each line.

For antipodal pairs on the unit sphere, the diameter is exactly 2.  If the largest absolute inner product between distinct line directions is `c`, the minimum squared distance among all 14 endpoints is `2 - 2c`, hence the squared min/max ratio is `(1-c)/2`.  Thus minimizing the maximum absolute line correlation directly optimizes the evaluator objective for this centrally symmetric 14-point family.

The replacement uses fixed-seed multi-start projected gradient descent on a smooth log-sum-exp approximation to maximum absolute correlation.  It uses only NumPy, maintains unit directions after every update, retains the best actual maximum-correlation candidate rather than merely the smooth surrogate optimum, and finally returns the seven directions together with their negatives.
